case_title: Sanjay Puran Bagde & Anr. v. The State of Maharashtra
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (accused are relatives of the deceased); prior enmity arising from an earlier incident, per the High Court's finding
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony of the victim's wife (PW-6), her statements under s.161 and s.164 CrPC, and the victim's statements to her; no dying declaration
aggravating_circumstances: Accused came to the spot around 3 a.m. with two of them carrying axes; the attack was premeditated; the victim was held while being attacked
trial_court_outcome: Convicted the two axe-wielding accused under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; acquitted the two appellants. Sentence not stated.
high_court_outcome: Appeal of convicted accused dismissed; State's appeal allowed and acquittal of the two appellants reversed
offence_finally_established: Murder under IPC s.302 read with s.34 (common intention)
neutral_facts: On the night of 2–3 November 2015, at about 3 a.m., the victim and his wife woke up. While the wife was preparing to cook, the victim went out to attend to the call of nature. The wife heard the victim shouting that four persons were attacking him. She ran to the spot and saw two of the accused assaulting the victim with an axe, while two other accused were holding him. On her raising a loud alarm, all of them ran away. She found the victim bleeding. He told her that four of them had caught hold of him and attacked him with an axe. She gave him water at his request, and neighbours carried him into the house. He was then taken to a hospital by auto, where he was declared dead. The reason for the assault was alleged to be an evil eye kept by the victim on the wife of one of the accused. The wife's statements were recorded under Section 161 and later Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. A first information report was registered on 3 November 2015 and, after investigation, a charge sheet was filed. Four persons were charged with murder read with common intention. The wife, as the only eyewitness, gave evidence of the incident as described. No dying declaration was recorded, as the victim was declared dead on arrival at the hospital.
physical_harm: Death of the victim after axe assault; found bleeding; declared brought dead at hospital
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.302 r/w s.34 IPC); 1 finally upheld against each appellant
premeditation_planning: Yes. The Court found the presence of the accused with axes at about 3 a.m. showed a premeditated intention.
motive: alleged: the victim allegedly kept an evil eye on the wife of one of the accused
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of the victim's wife (PW-6), including the victim's statements to her; identification of all accused; the manner of the incident
witness_credibility: PW-6 (wife) found reliable by both courts; no glaring inconsistency between her s.161 and s.164 CrPC statements; no quibble with the manner of the incident or identification of the accused
post_offence_conduct: Accused ran away when the wife raised a loud alarm; no other post-offence conduct noted
trial_duration: offence: night intervening 2nd and 3rd November 2015; trial judgment: 14.09.2017; High Court: 05.02.2019; Supreme Court: 28.07.2022
legal_representation: Appellants: Akash Kakade, Somanatha Padhan, Swetab Kumar, Ashok Anand, Rakesh Kr. Singh, Bipin Bihari Singh. State of Maharashtra (respondent): Rahul Chitnis, Sachin Patil, Aaditya A. Pande, Geo Joseph, Ms. Shwetal Shepal
investigation_status: FIR No. 79/2015 registered on 03.11.2015; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: two axe-wielding accused convicted under s.302 r/w s.34; two appellants acquitted. High Court: convicted accused's appeal dismissed; State's appeal allowed and the appellants' acquittal reversed. Supreme Court: SLP of the axe-wielding accused dismissed on 20.01.2020; appellants' appeal dismissed.
defence_argument: The appellants only held the victim while the other two attacked, so there was no shared common intention; counsel also sought a re-examination of the entire evidence
legal_principle_applied: Section 34 IPC: common intention requires a simultaneous consensus of minds and participation in the criminal act; participation need not be physical presence; s.34 imposes constructive liability
precedent_relied_upon: Jasdeep Singh Alias Jassu v. State of Punjab (2022) 2 SCC 545; Virendra Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (2010) 8 SCC 407
judicial_aggravating_factors: Premeditated attack with axes at about 3 a.m.; appellants held the victim while the others attacked, showing a shared intention
